survival.title: Korea Survival Guide
survival.subtitle: Everything foreign travelers need to know before and during their trip to Korea
survival.esimBody: Buy your eSIM online before flying. Activate it right as you land to have instant 4G/5G data.
survival.transitBody: Get a T-money card at airport convenience stores (CU, GS25) inside the arrivals terminal.
survival.appsBody: Download Naver Map (Google Maps doesn’t work), Papago for translations, and Kakao T for taxis.
survival.cardsBody: Visa and Mastercard are accepted almost everywhere (convenience stores, cafes, taxis, and sit-down dinners).
survival.cashBody: Traditional markets, street food stalls, and transit card recharges. Transit recharge kiosks only accept cash KRW.
survival.atmBody: Use ATMs marked with a Global ATM sign. Major banks like KB, Hana, and Shinhan have robust English interfaces.
survival.tmoneyBody: Tap when boarding and tap again when getting off subways or buses. Keep it topped up with cash at subway ticket machines.
survival.subwayBody: Subways are highly color-coded and announced in English. Follow transit arrows and check Naver Maps for correct exits.
survival.taxiBody: Hail standard orange or grey taxis. Show the driver your address written in Korean Hangul from Naver Maps.
survival.q1: Do I need cash in Korea?
survival.a1: Yes, you need a small amount of cash. While cards are accepted everywhere, you must recharge transit cards (T-money) with cash only. Street food stalls, local traditional markets, and some small businesses also require cash. We recommend carrying about 50,000 to 100,000 KRW in cash.
survival.q2: Can I use my foreign credit card?
survival.a2: Yes! Visa and Mastercard are accepted at 95% of businesses including convenience stores, taxis, restaurants, and cafes. Note that foreign-issued cards can occasionally be declined at older terminals, so carrying some cash is a smart backup plan.
survival.a3: In major tourist areas (Seoul, Busan, Jeju), signs and menus have English. Subway systems and buses are fully English-friendly. However, local shopkeepers and taxi drivers may not speak fluent English. Downloading translation apps like Papago is highly recommended.
survival.q4: Is Korea safe for solo female travelers?
survival.a4: South Korea is consistently ranked as one of the safest countries in the world. Crime rates are extremely low, and it is very safe to walk alone at night. Standard travel safety precautions still apply, but you can explore with peace of mind.
survival.q5: What apps do I need in Korea?
survival.a5: Three apps are absolutely mandatory: 1. Naver Map or KakaoMap (Google Maps does not work for walking directions), 2. Papago (the most accurate English-to-Korean translation app), and 3. Kakao T (for ordering taxis safely).

about.heroSubtitle: Empowering foreign independent travelers to explore Korea worry-free
about.missionBody: gokoreamate is an AI-powered travel guide designed specifically for foreign travelers visiting Korea. We help you plan your trip, find solo-friendly spots, and navigate Korea without getting stuck.
about.dataBodyBefore: Local information is provided by the Korea Tourism Organization (
about.dataBodyAfter: ) through their TourAPI. We verify and curate locations to make sure accessibility features, payment guidelines, and solo-friendly attributes are completely transparent.
about.aiBody: Itineraries and blog posts are put together with AI assistance. We aim for accurate, well-organized guidance, but local operations change — please verify important details before your trip.
about.contactBody: Have feedback or suggestions? We'd love to hear from you. Feel free to contact our team to share your thoughts or report details that need updates. Together, let's make traveling in Korea an unforgettable experience!
about.footerNote: Place data provided by the Korea Tourism Organization. Trip planning powered by AI.

auth.deleteAccountBody:
Deleted: your trips with photos & notes, saved places, My Places, likes/dislikes, 'helpful' marks, event reactions, place suggestions under review, This Trip sync data, device links and consent records, and the login account.
Kept: copies others already made (link removed), anonymous statistics, suggestions already adopted as public places, and inquiry/report records (separate retention).
This cannot be undone.

auth.deleteIdentityVerified: Identity verified — you can delete with the button below (valid for 10 minutes).
auth.deleteFailed: Couldn't delete. Try the same button again shortly — it resumes from what's left.

analyticsConsent.title: Usage statistics consent (optional)
analyticsConsent.intro: These statistics help us improve the service. Every feature works the same if you don't agree. Statistics turn on only if you agree to both items below.
analyticsConsent.collectLabel: [Optional] Consent to collection and use of personal information
analyticsConsent.collectDetails: Items: a cookie identifier, screens viewed and features used (city and public-place level), device and browser information, IP address · Purpose: usage statistics and service improvement · Kept (user- and event-level data): events 2 months, user data 14 months (reset on new activity) · Refusing has no disadvantage.
analyticsConsent.transferLabel: [Optional] Consent to transfer of personal information outside Korea
analyticsConsent.transferDetails: Recipient: Google LLC (USA), contact support.google.com/policies · Items transferred: the items above · When and how: each time you use the service, over an encrypted connection · Recipient's purpose and retention: providing usage statistics, events 2 months, user data 14 months (user- and event-level data, reset on new activity) · How to refuse and effect: leave it unchecked or turn it off later and nothing is sent; the service is not affected.
analyticsConsent.footer: If you are under 14, please don't agree. You can change or withdraw your choice at any time under More › Usage statistics. Withdrawing stops sending from then on and deletes the GA cookies this service set in this browser. Information already sent is not deleted immediately; user- and event-level data follow the retention settings above (they do not apply to standard aggregated reports).
analyticsConsent.cardTitle: Choose whether to send usage statistics
analyticsConsent.cardBody: To improve the service, we can send usage statistics to Google Analytics (USA). Every feature works the same if you refuse.
analyticsConsent.liveOne: Only one item is selected — statistics need both, so they stay off even if you save.
analyticsConsent.statusPartial: Off · only one item agreed (both are needed)
analyticsConsent.noticeBody: You can choose whether to send usage statistics to Google Analytics (USA). Every feature works the same if you refuse or don't choose, and you can change it later under More › Usage statistics.

journey.importCannot: pages that need a login, private chat addresses (not share links), files
journey.importNeedLogin: Import needs sign-in. Import analysis uses your free AI trip building (1 per month, shared with AI planning, plus 1 extra the first time).
journey.importOutside: Places outside our 5 cities can also be saved or imported and used in your trip.

pickCity.name: Pick a city

pickCourse.name: Pick a course

adoptCourse.name: Use this course

adoptDates.name: Set dates and create

pickPlace.name: Pick a place

addToThisTrip.name: Add to This Trip

buildTrip.say: Tap this to build the trip
buildTrip.name: Build the trip
buildTrip.missing: This Trip is empty — add places first

pasteLink.name: Paste text or a link

pasteLink.say_tut-import-text: Paste the plan you copied from Gemini, ChatGPT or elsewhere here

reviewImport.say: Check it, then tap this to create your trip
reviewImport.name: Review and save
reviewImport.why: Places not in our list (including outside our 5 cities) are kept as your places, not dropped.

reviewImport.say_tut-import-multi-trip: Tap [Start a new trip with these places]

openMyTrip.name: Open my trip

checkDates.name: Check dates

addRecord.say: At a place, tap this on its card to add a photo or note
addRecord.name: Add a photo or note
addRecord.why: No photos yet? That's fine — pause with [Continue during my trip] and pick up here later.
addRecord.say_tut-itinerary-tab: Photos and notes go on each place card in [Itinerary] — tap the [Itinerary] tab

openStory.name: Open Story
openStory.why: Your plan and records shown as one story.

publishStory.say: See what will be shown, then decide yourself whether to publish
publishStory.name: Decide to publish
publishStory.why: You don't have to publish. Only records you tick are shown — show-off needs at least one public record.

makeShareCard.name: Make a share card
makeShareCard.why: The card shows title, dates, city and photos — no exact address or map.
makeShareCard.missing: Share cards are for published trips — you can skip this

shareCard.say: Share it or save the image — you decide where it goes
shareCard.name: Share or save the card
shareCard.why: Nothing is posted automatically — you pick the app in your phone's share sheet.

submitRecommend.say: Show off your trip — submit it to the local recommendations
submitRecommend.name: Show off your trip
submitRecommend.why: After review it appears as a recommendation to other travelers — posted on the site, unlike the share card.
submitRecommend.missing: This appears once the trip is public with 3+ places and one public record — you can skip it

fullTripAi.heading: Write the whole trip at once
fullTripAi.desc: Tap this once your plan and records are in. In one request, the AI reads your record photos (the first photo of each record) together with places, dates and your own notes, and suggests a trip title, story intro and a title and text for every record in three styles.

fullTripAi.needLogin: AI writing needs sign-in. Writing it yourself works without signing in.
